drills.title: Turn and attack (GRUT)
drills.description:
A focus drill for attacking a disc you didn't see thrown: the reaction a cutter needs when a disc goes up unexpectedly.

**How it runs**

1. Pairs. The receiver stands with their back to the thrower.
2. The thrower puts up a floaty disc a little away from the receiver and calls "Up!".
3. The receiver turns, finds the disc over their shoulder and attacks it.

**Coaching points**

- Stay on your toes before the call.
- Look back over your shoulder to find the disc.
- Get in front of the disc: attack it, don't wait for it to come to you.

**Harder**

- The thrower varies height, distance and side.
- The receiver must catch at the highest point they can reach.
- Add a defender who also turns on "Up!" to make it a 50/50 contest (week 25, aerial contests).
drills.setup_instructions: Pairs with one disc, 10-15 m apart; receiver faces away from the thrower.

drills.title: Rinkydink (GRUT)
drills.description:
A pre-game focus drill that gets hands ready for imperfect throws, and loosens players up so they aren't tight before a game.

**How it runs**

- Partners throw to each other deliberately badly: wobbly, odd spin, odd angles, "a little bit funny".
- The receiver catches one-handed at the rim, or two-handed with the difficulty turned up.

**Coaching points**

- Stay relaxed and have fun: the aim is to loosen up, not to be perfect.
- Watch the disc all the way in, however it is spinning.

**Use it** at the end of the game-day warm-up, before the 4v3 mini.
drills.setup_instructions: Pairs with one disc, 5-8 m apart.

drills.title: 10-minute low-release session (GRUT)
drills.description:
Seven throwing variations to do once a week. They build comfort with low releases and control of the disc's nose angle.

**The seven variations** (a few throws each, both forehand and backhand)

1. **Squat:** throw from a squat and release below the knee.
2. **Squat and pause:** the same, but pause at the bottom before you throw.
3. **Wrist scrape:** try to scrape your wrist on the ground as you throw, the lowest release possible.
4. **Snap back:** pull your wrist back straight after the throw.
5. **Low and flat:** release as low as possible with the nose as flat as possible.
6. **Low and nose up:** low release with an extreme nose up; this gives touch.
7. **The perfect throw:** nose angle in between, straight into the receiver's hands.

**Links to the plan:** wide and low releases (Card 7, week 10) and throwing in the wind (Card 12): variations 5 and 6 are the controls behind "low into it, high with it". Good for the home programme.
drills.setup_instructions: Pairs with one disc, about 10 m apart.

drills.title: 20-20-20 (GRUT)
drills.description:
A competitive throwing drill: focused throws at three distances, adjusted to the cutter, with a reset if anyone drops.

**Set-up:** four cones close together in a box. Two lines stand behind the two front cones, facing upfield. One cone has a thrower with the disc and another is where the cutter starts. The cutter runs to the third cone and the thrower follows to the fourth, so the drill keeps flowing.

**Stages**

1. **Stage 1:** 20 completions in a row without a drop.
2. **Stage 2:** move the cones 3 m wider and the upfield cones about 5 m further upfield, then another 20.
3. **Stage 3:** throw from the same cones into the endzone. Every throw must be a score or it counts as a drop.

**Rule:** any drop sends the group back to stage 1. You win by clearing all three stages without a drop.

**Format:** race the clock with one set, or race the other half of the field with two sets.

**2s version:** 10-10-10, or a drop sends you back one stage rather than to stage 1.

*Check the video for the exact cutting pattern before running it.*
drills.setup_instructions: Four cones in a small box near an endzone; two lines behind the front cones. Two sets for a race.

drills.title: Under-to-away lead passes (GRUT)
drills.description:
Two variations for throwing better leading passes, and throws that sit in front of the receiver.

**Set-up:** three players: a thrower with a static mark, and a cutter starting at a cone. The cutter can point to the side they'll cut to, to help the thrower; leave the point out to train reaction and release speed.

**The cut:** a hard jab in, so the thrower can read the cutter's speed. Then a hard turn and a few sprint steps to the catch.

**The perfect throw has**

1. **Height:** always at a catchable height.
2. **Angle:** "don't cheat". Keep the angle small so the disc sits in front of the receiver instead of arriving across them.
3. **Speed:** always in front of the receiver, never behind, and not too far to the side.

**Tip:** to make the disc sit, throw with the nose a little more up and plenty of spin.

**Variations**

- **Easier:** the receiver opens to the side away from the throw, giving more space to run onto it.
- **Sideline:** the cut runs along a line of cones (the sideline) and the disc must stay in.
- **Target boxes:** set boxes close, far, or very close and very fast to practise a specific throw.
drills.setup_instructions: Groups of three (thrower, mark, cutter); one cone for the cutter's start, a cone line for the sideline variation.

drills.title: Leading pass drill (GRUT)
drills.description:
A continuous dish-and-upline pattern for give-and-go and leading passes.

**How it runs**

1. The player who has just caught throws a little dish to a partner.
2. She runs across, gets the dish back, and throws a leading upline pass to the other side.
3. The receiver there catches the dish from that side, and the pattern repeats. Lines wait at each end; switch sides after a few minutes.

**Communication version:** the dish thrower calls whether she is going **in front** of or **behind** the receiver.

**Size:** run it big for long leading passes, or make it much smaller to practise small ball.
drills.setup_instructions: Two lines facing each other about 15-20 m apart, plus a dish partner at each end.

drills.title: Tap-in (GRUT)
drills.description:
A 2v1 small-ball game from Kristyna Tlustá, GRUT's small-ball specialist: small passes, knowing when to stop the give-and-go, and scoring from a 1v1.

**Set-up:** two attackers and one defender. Cones mark a sideline, and tiny cones mark a very small endzone box.

**How it runs**

1. The attacker on the right starts by attacking the defender ("tapping her in").
2. The two attackers then play to score in the box.
3. **Defence:** don't mark. Go to whichever attacker is open and defend her.
4. **Stall:** 4, counted from the sideline.

**Coaching points**

- Small, quick passes.
- Know when to stop the give-and-go and attack the score.
- Win the 1v1 at the end.

**2s version:** stall 6, or 3v2.
drills.setup_instructions: A small channel along a sideline with a tiny endzone box at one end; groups of three.

drills.title: Breakside flow (GRUT)
drills.description:
A team drill for opening up the break side and keeping the flow going there. "Having the ability as a team to open up the break side and create break-side flow is very important since it opens up the whole field."

**How it runs**

1. The thrower breaks the backhand force to the first cutter, who has started the swing.
2. As the first cutter catches, the second cutter leaves for the next swing. Don't go too early.
3. If the break isn't on, still run the break-side flow, but time it off the reset: dump, then swing.

**Links to the plan:** option 3 is the dynamic dump and Jedi in action (Cards 1 and 22), and the drill is Card 7's "a break should lead to a throw that gains yards next".
drills.setup_instructions: A thrower with a mark forcing backhand, a dump, and two lines of break-side cutters.

drills.title: Read-the-defender hucking (GRUT)
drills.description:
An advanced hucking drill: the thrower reads the deep defender's position and picks the huck that goes where the defender can't get to.

**Set-up**

- The thrower is on the sideline with the disc.
- A second player stands next to her and runs an upline cut.
- One deep cutter runs deep.
- The deep cutter's defender stands on one of three cones and doesn't defend; their position is the cue.

**The read** (left and right as seen in the video; mirror it on the other sideline)

| Defender on | Throw |
| --- | --- |
| Left cone | Straight huck |
| Middle cone | Huck to the middle of the endzone |
| Right cone | Blade to the left side of the endzone |

**Progressions**

1. The defender moves to a cone late, as the thrower winds up.
2. The upline cutter is a live option: if the huck isn't there, hit the upline.
3. The defender is live.

**2s version:** straight and middle options only.
drills.setup_instructions: A thrower on the sideline, an upline cutter beside her, a deep cutter, and three cones for the defender about 25 m downfield.
